title: Soft-hedge regional escalator for stream stability
creator: Priya Srinivasan
description: Design and implement a ‘soft-hedge escalator’ at the hosted API edge/gateway to enable active-active multi-region cutovers for streaming and sessionful requests without violating SLOs. The escalator mixes small hedged duplicates to target regions, measures end-to-end stream stability and token latency, and escalates traffic using headroom-aware gates and circuit-breakers. It must preserve session affinity for non-idempotent streams where possible, avoid double-charging customers, and integrate with existing KV prefix caching and rollout policies.
background_and_motivation: We need a migration mechanism that can move live streaming sessions between regions with minimal token loss and bounded SLO impact. Existing hard-cutover approaches either cause token replays, broken streams, or significant latency spikes. The soft-hedge escalator aims to mitigate these by: 1) running hedged mirrors for a fraction of requests, 2) observing stream commit/close and early-loss signals, 3) progressively shifting traffic while using circuit-breakers and load-shedding to protect tail SLOs.
design_notes: Hedged fanout model: for a configurable fraction f of session starts, send parallel requests to primary and candidate region; pick the first successful response for non-streaming requests and attach a passive mirror for streaming sessions to observe throughput/latency without completing client-visible outputs.
Soft-escalator phases: observe -> hedge-and-measure -> gated-increment -> handover. Each phase has time and success rate thresholds tied to SLO headroom metrics.

Circuit breakers: two-layer breakers - local per-edge breaker (fast, small window) and regional breaker (aggregated, longer window). Breaker trips are surfaced to escalator which reduces increment steps and increases hedged sampling.

Session continuity: for streaming sessions we keep a lightweight token that allows reconnection to same backend if handover fails; when hard handover is necessary, we prefer draining secondary replicas via KV-snapshot/offset and use prefix/KV cache to rehydrate state in target region.

Billing: to avoid double-billing, mirrored requests are marked with a non-billable header and recorded separately; only winner responses counted. For long-running mirrored streams we sample only metadata (latency, error codes) rather than full tokens.
Telemetry hooks: emit events for hedged-start, mirror-pulse, escalate-step, breaker-trip, shed-rate, and final-cutover with per-request tags (region, model, model-version, route).
Rollout safety: default strategy is 1% sample hedging with slow ramp to 20% over automated policy; require manual approval for >20% for the first customer cohorts.
Fallbacks: if candidate region experiences cold-start prewarming penalty, escalator backoffs and reverts to primary using a probabilistic backoff to avoid oscillation.
Compatibility: must work with streaming SDKs (gRPC + WebSocket), function-calling, and structured-output flows; streaming mirror is metadata-only by default to reduce egress cost.
Operational controls: admin flags to force-disable hedging per-customer, per-route, or globally; thresholds adjustable via console and infra config.
Trade-offs: mirrors introduce extra load; we limit mirror sampling to preserve headroom. More aggressive hedging improves safety but increases cost and potential contention on model shards.
acceptance_criteria: Implement hedged fanout plumbing in gateway for both unary and streaming requests with non-billable mirror tagging
Escalator phases implemented with configurable thresholds and observability hooks
Two-layer circuit breakers integrated and tripping reduces escalation steps automatically
Session continuity mechanism for streaming reattaches works for >95% of simulated cutovers in test harness
End-to-end SLO regressions limited to <5% of historical 99th latency SLA during controlled cutover experiments
Cost telemetry shows mirrored sampling under budget for first-phase rollout (<= +8% inference tokens for sampled customers)
Runbook updated and a chaos test (regional failure) demonstrates graceful failback without token duplication for at least 90% of sessions
implementation_plan: Phase 0: Experiments — add mirror metadata plumbing and lightweight mirror agent that only records latency/errors (2 weeks)
Phase 1: Hedged fanout — add parallel-start logic and winner selection for unary flows; mirror-only mode for streaming starts (3 weeks)
Phase 2: Escalator controller — implement phased gate state machine + thresholds + integration with circuit breakers and KV cache gating (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Session continuity — implement reattach token and KV snapshot transfer primitives (3 weeks)
Phase 4: Observability & Safety — dashboards, alerts, and admin flags; end-to-end tests and canary rollout (2 weeks)
Phase 5: Rollout — opt-in customers -> gradual expansion -> manual approval for global by SRE/Product (ongoing)
Estimated total dev time: 12 weeks across infra, runtime, and gateway teams
testing_plan: Unit tests for mirror tagging and winner selection logic
Integration tests: synthetic streaming sessions across 2 regions validating reattach token semantics
Chaos tests: simulate regional latency spike and failover; measure token loss and error surface
Load test: hedged sampling at 20% for 30m to validate headroom calculations and breaker behavior
SLO evaluation harness: automated backtests against recent production traffic traces to assert <=5% 99th latency impact
Billing sanity checks to ensure mirrored requests are excluded from billable counts
rollout_plan: Canary cohort: 5 internal prod-like customers on dedicated routes with hedging=1% for 48h
Observe metrics and SRE sign-off -> increase to 5% for additional 72h
Enable streaming mirror for canary cohort and run chaos scenario (region prewarm/eviction)
If metrics stable, auto-escalate sample rate to 20% for beta cohort; require PM + SRE approval to go further
Global rollout gated on cost and SLO objectives and a final exec signoff for hosted API paths
telemetry_and_alerting: Metrics to emit: hedged_start_rate, mirror_success_rate, mirror_latency_p50/p95/p99, escalate_step_progress, local_breaker_trips, regional_breaker_trips, shed_rate_per_route, session_reattach_success_rate
Dashboards: per-region SLO headroom, hedged-sample impact, and mirrored traffic cost delta
Alerts: breaker_trip_rate > 0.5% over 5m, session_reattach_success_rate < 90% over 10m, escalate_step_failure_ratio > 2%
Tracing: link hedged-start and winner decision to request trace ids to debug doubled or delayed responses
risk_and_mitigations: Increased model load from mirrors — mitigation: strict sampling cap, mirror metadata-only for streams, enforce circuit-breaker caps
Oscillation between regions during noisy conditions — mitigation: hysteresis on escalator steps and additive backoff on repeated failures
Potential double-charges if billing marking fails — mitigation: conservative rollout, billing integration tests, and temporary billing hold for canary customers
Edge-state divergence on KV caches causing poor reattach — mitigation: snapshot-and-verify step and KV prewarm thresholds before final handover
